page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-2 is a general-purpose compute instance configured with a compute-leaning resource ratio. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core across two hardware threads on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.2 GHz. The CPU cache architecture comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 16 MB L3 cache. Instruction set support includes AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, while advanced vector extensions such as AVX-512 and matrix engines like AMX are absent.

System memory is limited to 2.0 GB of RAM, yielding an allocation of 1.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, requiring workloads to rely on remote block storage for persistence. Network connectivity provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating network address translation or provisioned IP configurations for public internet egress.

Benchmark results situate the e2-highcpu-2 in the entry-level performance tier. Compute testing records a Geekbench single-core score of 906.0 and a multi-core score of 1073.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 1664.25. Memory bandwidth reaches 13.03 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 11.11 GB/sec for writes. Application-level metrics demonstrate 1.34 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 1.39 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

Due to its restricted 2.0 GB memory footprint and baseline compute capacity, the instance is positioned as an economical option for lightweight services rather than resource-heavy pipelines. It is suited for basic web serving, lightweight microservices, testing environments, and non-memory-intensive batch processing.

Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the processor features 16 MB of L3 cache with hardware support for AVX, AES, and bit manipulation instructions, but omits AVX-512 extensions. The instance includes no bundled local storage, no hardware GPU accelerators, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark performance places the instance in the lower percentiles, producing a Geekbench multi-core score of 1073.0, uncached memory read bandwidth of 13.03 GB/sec, and 1.34 million Redis SET operations per second. With an allocation of 1.0 GB RAM per vCPU, the instance delivers a low-cost profile suited for lightweight application hosting, staging tasks, and basic background worker jobs.
